description: Crew Health Ops 🛰️ is a 3D health monitor that helps astronauts read their own health and act first when Earth is minutes away. Five body sites (sleep & mood, temperature, heart rate & BP, blood sugar, radiation) turn OK, Watch or Act, each with guidance and a path to the flight surgeon. Space-station radiation uses real NASA OSDR RadLab ISS data. Team: Edmund Anthony & Nandani Chauhan. Live: edmundzen.github.io/crew-health-ops
summary: We built Crew Health Ops, a 3D web app that helps astronauts read their own health and act first when Earth is minutes away. It addresses the challenge by gathering six health indicators (sleep, mood, body temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar) plus radiation dose and showing them on an interactive astronaut whose body sites turn green (OK), amber (Watch) or red (Act). Each site explains what the reading means, which spaceflight hazard drives it, what to do now, and when to escalate to the flight surgeon. Alerts never clear themselves, and every action is logged on a 30-day mission timeline. This matters because on a Mars mission a message to Earth can take up to 22 minutes each way, so crews must assess and act on their own health first. Space-station radiation uses real NASA OSDR RadLab ISS data.
details:
WHAT IT DOES: A 3D astronaut with five clickable health sites: head (sleep, mood), forehead (body temperature), heart (heart rate, blood pressure), left arm (blood sugar) and a dosimeter (radiation). Each site shows today's reading, a 10-day trend against the crew member's own baseline, and a guidance card: what it is, which of NASA's five spaceflight hazards drives it, what to do now, and when to escalate. Alerts move Open → Acknowledged → Escalated and never clear themselves.

FEATURES: 4 fictional crew with personalities that explain their health stories (a night-owl engineer's sleep debt raises his heart rate); 5 locations (space station, lunar orbit, Mars transit, Moon base, Mars base) where the astronaut floats or walks and the message delay to Earth changes (seconds to ~22 minutes each way); mission-day slider; guided daily check; 30-day mission timeline; 60-second self-check that updates the readings.

IMPACT: Gives crews on deep-space missions the ability to understand and act on their own health before Earth can reply. The same approach could help remote clinics on Earth with little access to doctors.

CREATIVITY: Health status is shown on the body itself, the astronaut physically holds the problem area when an alert reaches Act, and the crew's personalities turn data into a story judges can follow.

TOOLS: Three.js (3D), HTML/CSS/JavaScript, GitHub Pages hosting. Built with Claude as an AI coding assistant. User manual and code: https://github.com/edmundzen/crew-health-ops

FACTORS CONSIDERED: Real vs simulated data is clearly labelled; alert thresholds are prototype design choices informed by NASA HRP material, not clinical limits; a human always decides (Acknowledge/Escalate).
